prerequisites: Basic knowledge of materials engineering for plastics and metals

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire broad knowledge for determining technological material characteristic values of metals and plastics. They understand the relationships between testing methods and static, cyclic, and dynamic characteristic values and can interpret them.

Students possess detailed knowledge and understanding in the field of materials testing, corresponding to the current state of knowledge and research. They have basic knowledge of testing procedures used in industry for quality assurance.

Students are able to define test procedures considering relevant standards, coordinate sample preparation, monitor test execution, and document it appropriately. They can discuss, interpret material behavior based on test results, and provide corresponding instructions given a scientific question.
Students are able to analyze and interpret data sets and test results obtained through measurements and derive corresponding instructions given a scientific question.
With the knowledge acquired in the module, students are able to develop solutions to investigate material-specific questions using suitable experiments.
Students can present their work results from the laboratory practical in a clearly structured written form and respond orally to queries.

syllabus_topics: Motivation and purpose of materials testing
Mechanical properties: Tensile test, bending test, hardness test, impact test, static long-term stress, fatigue test
Non-destructive testing methods: Ultrasonic testing, eddy current testing, X-ray testing
Thermal properties: DSC, TGA, TMA, heat deflection temperature, test methods for determining flow properties
assessment_rules: The choice of examination type (experimental work or oral exam) is at the discretion of the examiners and will be communicated at the beginning of the semester. If experimental work is chosen as the graded assessment, it will not be part of the ungraded assessment. If an oral examination is chosen as the graded assessment, experimental work will be chosen as the ungraded assessment. Regular attendance requires participation in at least 80% of the course.
